title: OSCE Clinical Reasoning & Bias Evaluation Rubric
subtitle: Standardized Patient Simulation Framework | Assessing Cognitive, Diagnostic, and Interpersonal Biases

source.file: OSCE Cognitive & Interpersonal Bias Evaluation Rubric.pdf

evaluatorInstructions: This rubric is designed to assess medical students during complex standardized patient encounters (e.g., Denise Vance case: acute chest pain with comorbid GAD and triage framing risks). Score students across the five core cognitive error categories using the 1–4 scale below.

categories.name: Premature Closure & Anchoring
categories.target: Locks onto initial diagnosis early; ignores evolving clinical data or physical exam findings.

descriptors.1: Fixates on initial impression; fails to adjust reasoning.
descriptors.2: Considers alternates only when explicitly prompted.
descriptors.3: Actively updates differential as new data emerge.
descriptors.4: Performs diagnostic time-outs; systematically revises differential.

categories.name: Confirmation & Search Bias
categories.target: Asks leading questions supporting the leading hypothesis; skips disconfirming evidence.

descriptors.1: Asks leading questions; ignores contradictory symptoms.
descriptors.3: Asks balanced positive and negative predictive questions.
descriptors.4: Probes for key negatives and red flags ruling out alternatives.

categories.name: Implicit Demographic Bias
categories.target: Assumptions based on race, gender, age, socioeconomic status, or mental health history.

descriptors.1: Uses dismissive language; attributes symptoms solely to lifestyle.
descriptors.4: Actively counteracts bias; addresses social determinants equitably.

categories.name: Framing & Availability
categories.target: Influenced by sign-out framing, recent patient encounters, or emotional recall.

descriptors.1: Accepts handoff label uncritically without baseline inquiry.
descriptors.2: Mentions framing but struggles to decouple from case.
descriptors.3: Distinguishes current presentation from previous cases.
descriptors.4: Identifies framing risks; evaluates from first principles.

categories.name: Diagnostic Attribution
categories.target: Attributes complex somatic complaints entirely to psychiatric history or chronic illness.

descriptors.1: Dismisses new symptoms as psychological without workup.
descriptors.2: Investigates minimally before attributing to baseline.
descriptors.4: Rigorously separates acute pathology from baseline history.

applicationPolicy.notObservable: Not observable is an application extension, not a rating in the supplied PDF. Use null with an explanation when the case or transcript cannot support a category; do not fabricate a 1–4 rating.
applicationPolicy.totals: The source provides no aggregate score, bias percentage, pass/fail cutoff or demographic causality test. Do not add one.
applicationPolicy.audience: Faculty only; separate from the seven-domain student assessment.
applicationPolicy.indicators: Ratings 1 or 2 are flagged for faculty review by the application. This is not a source-defined bias diagnosis or pass/fail cutoff.
applicationPolicy.groupUse: Apply the five-category matrix separately to each completed trial. Cross-trial observations are additional evidence for faculty review, not proof of bias.
